A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 15 pages of each version, including the supplementary material, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-training experiments on CIFAR-10, CelebA-HQ, and ImageNet, including FID comparisons, gradient analyses, and a timestep-subset ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, quantitative comparisons, analyses, and generated-image examples in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same adaptive Beta-distribution sampler, sampler update, and timestep-subset approximation. The new appendix paragraph specifies the existing feature-selection implementation rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 32×32, CelebA-HQ 256×256, and ImageNet 256×256, retaining the same image-generation tasks and noise-schedule coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain DDPM/LDM, P2, Min-SNR, Log-normal, and SpeeD in their corresponding comparisons. Tables 3–4 retain the Min-SNR compatibility comparison and gradient-variance-proportional sampling comparator.

E3.justification: Table 7 replaces the single timestep-sampler learning-rate entry of 1e-2 with 1e-2 for linear/quadratic schedules and 1e-3 for cosine. This is a limited revision to reported training settings, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Evaluation metrics, sample counts, and reported budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The gradient-variance and timestep-interdependence analyses, sampling-distribution visualizations, variance-based sampling comparison, and subset-size ablation remain unchanged. The appendix retains the same generated-image examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark uncertainty through repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly described F-statistic is a feature-selection criterion, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: In Table 1, SpeeD's CIFAR-10 FID for the cosine schedule at 0.6M iterations changes from 4.57 to 3.57, placing it ahead of Log-normal's unchanged 3.78. The proposed method remains at 3.00 in that column. Other numerical results and plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, Theorem 1, the timestep-independence assumption, and the appendix computational-overhead derivation are unchanged. The feature-selection clarification adds no formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient-variance bottlenecks, adaptive timestep sampling, faster convergence, and robustness across experimental settings.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the interpretations concerning timestep interdependence, adaptive sampling, and compatibility with heuristic weighting. The limitations concerning computational overhead and unexplored applicability to score-based diffusion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies linear-regression F-statistic feature selection, adds CIFAR-10 sampler hidden depth 2, and revises its learning-rate documentation. It removes sampler gradient-norm entries from Tables 7–8 and sampler optimizer/beta entries from Tables 8–9. Section 6 changes four RTX 3090 GPUs to RTX 4090 GPUs without a count, while the appendix still specifies four RTX 3090 GPUs. These omissions do not establish that the corresponding operations were disabled.

R1.justification: The same 35 cited works and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against heuristic timestep weighting/sampling and learning-to-optimize research is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations and contribution footnotes, adds an acknowledgements section and a feature-selection paragraph, and renumbers appendix sections and cross-references. The main scientific narrative is otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: All eight figures and nine tables are retained. Table 7 becomes wider and moves downward beneath the new paragraph; Tables 7–9 have added or removed parameter rows. References reflow and printed page numbers disappear, while the figures retain their designs.

improvement.justification: v2 improves documentation of feature selection and CIFAR-10 sampler configuration, but removes optimizer and gradient-norm information and introduces conflicting RTX 4090/3090 hardware descriptions. The scientific evidence is otherwise retained apart from one revised baseline score. These gains and losses affect reproducibility in opposing ways, and the PDFs do not resolve the conflicting settings well enough to establish a reliable net quality improvement.
